title: Te Aro Astanga Yoga vs Run Pōneke – Which Wellington Gym Is Right for You?
meta_desc: Compare Te Aro Astanga Yoga and Run Pōneke NZ on price, contracts, facilities, 24/7 access and value. Find the best fit for your fitness goals in Wellington.
intro: Both Te Aro Astanga Yoga and Run Pōneke NZ offer community‑focused, no‑contract options in Wellington, but they serve very different practitioners. This guide breaks down the key differences so you can pick the right hub for your routine.

sections.heading: Pricing & Contract Details
sections.body: Te Aro Astanga Yoga charges $15–$30 per week depending on class frequency, with no joining fee and no lock‑in contract. Run Pōneke NZ ranges from $15–$40 per week, also fee‑free and contract‑free, but pricing varies by session type and membership tier. Both gyms let you cancel at any time, but Run Pōneke’s higher ceiling reflects its additional recovery facilities.
list: Te Aro Astanga Yoga: $15–$30 / week, $0 joining fee, no contract.
Run Pōneke NZ: $15–$40 / week, $0 joining fee, no contract.
Both allow month‑to‑month cancellation with 24‑hour notice.

sections.heading: Facilities & 24/7 Access
sections.body: Astanga Yoga provides a calm studio with heated floors, yoga props and a small lounge. There is no 24/7 access – classes run on a set schedule. Run Pōneke offers a larger suite of amenities: three infrared saunas, two 5 °C cold‑plunge pools, massage rooms and mobility pods. Access is limited to opening hours (typically 6 am–9 pm), not round‑the‑clock.
list: Te Aro Astanga – focused studio space, no extra recovery gear.
Run Pōneke – saunas, cold plunges, massage, mobility pods.
Neither provides 24/7 access; both operate within regular opening times.

sections.heading: Location & Community Vibe
sections.body: Te Aro Astanga Yoga sits in Wellington’s Te Aro neighbourhood, offering a tranquil, traditional Ashtanga environment. The community is tight‑knit, attracting long‑term practitioners who value discipline over casual flow. Run Pōneke NZ is located on the iconic Clyde Quay Wharf, giving members waterfront views and a social runner’s hub. The vibe is energetic, with group runs, recovery socials and a strong emphasis on community support.

rows: Infrared saunas, cold plunge, massage, mobility pods

sections.heading: Verdict – Who Should Join Which?
sections.body: If your primary goal is a disciplined, traditional Ashtanga practice in a calm, teacher‑led environment, Te Aro Astanga Yoga offers the best value – especially at the lower $15 / week tier. For runners, triathletes or anyone craving extensive recovery amenities, Run Pōneke NZ justifies its higher price with saunas, cold plunges and a vibrant waterfront community. Both gyms qualify for the Exercise NZ subsidy, so eligible members can shave 40–70 % off the weekly rate, making either option even more affordable.
list: Choose Te Aro Astanga Yoga if you want focused yoga without extra frills.
Choose Run Pōneke NZ if you need running groups, recovery facilities, and a social fitness hub.
